exercises.name: Push Up
exercises.description: The most fundamental upper body exercise. Builds chest, triceps and shoulder strength using nothing but your bodyweight.
instructions: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder width
Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe
Lower your chest to just above the floor
Push back up to the starting position
Keep your core tight throughout
coaching_cues: Chest to floor — not just halfway
Elbows at 45 degrees — not flared out wide
Squeeze your glutes to keep your body straight

exercises.name: Wide Push Up
exercises.description: A push up with a wider hand placement that shifts more focus onto the outer chest.
instructions: Start in a plank position with hands wider than shoulder width
Lower your chest toward the floor
Push back up squeezing your chest at the top
Keep core tight throughout
coaching_cues: The wider your hands the more you feel it in your chest
Do not let your hips sag
Full range of motion — chest nearly touching the floor

exercises.name: Diamond Push Up
exercises.description: A narrow push up variation that heavily targets the triceps and inner chest.
instructions: Form a diamond shape with your index fingers and thumbs
Place hands in the centre of your chest on the floor
Lower your chest toward your hands
Push back up keeping elbows close to your body
coaching_cues: Keep elbows pointing back — not flaring out
This is harder than a regular push up — reduce reps if needed
Feel the burn in your triceps at the top

exercises.name: Dumbbell Chest Press
exercises.description: A classic chest pressing movement using dumbbells. Allows a greater range of motion than a barbell.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench or floor with a dumbbell in each hand
Hold dumbbells at chest level with palms facing forward
Press the dumbbells up until arms are fully extended
Slowly lower back down to chest level
Keep core tight throughout
coaching_cues: Lower the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your chest
Press in a slight arc — not straight up
Control the weight on the way down

exercises.name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation movement that stretches and squeezes the chest through a wide arc of motion.
instructions: Lie flat with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest
With a slight bend in your elbows open your arms wide
Feel the stretch across your chest at the bottom
Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest
Squeeze your chest at the top
coaching_cues: Think of hugging a big tree
Never fully lock out your elbows
The stretch at the bottom is where the growth happens

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Press
exercises.description: An incline pressing movement that targets the upper chest for a fuller, more developed look.
instructions: Set a bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline
Hold dumbbells at shoulder level with palms forward
Press the dumbbells up and slightly together
Slowly lower back down to shoulder level
coaching_cues: Do not set the incline too steep — 30 to 45 degrees is ideal
Upper chest should be doing the work — not your shoulders
Full stretch at the bottom

exercises.name: Band Chest Press
exercises.description: A chest press using a resistance band anchored behind you. Great for home training.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height
Hold one end in each hand at chest level
Press forward until arms are fully extended
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: The more tension in the band the harder it gets
Squeeze your chest at full extension
Keep your core tight — do not arch your back

exercises.name: Band Chest Fly
exercises.description: A band variation of the chest fly. Provides constant tension for great chest activation.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height
Hold one end in each hand with arms wide
Bring your hands together in front of your chest
Slowly return to the wide starting position
coaching_cues: Slight bend in elbows throughout
Feel the squeeze when your hands meet
Control the band on the way back

exercises.name: Band Crossover
exercises.description: Mimics the cable crossover machine using a band. Great for targeting the inner chest.
instructions: Anchor band at shoulder height on one side
Hold the band with the opposite hand
Pull the band across your body in a sweeping arc
Return slowly to the starting position
Complete all reps then switch sides
coaching_cues: Think of sweeping the band toward your opposite hip
Slight forward lean helps engage the chest
Do not use your back — chest does the work

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: The king of chest exercises. A compound pressing movement that builds serious chest size and strength.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with eyes under the bar
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width
Unrack the bar and lower it to your mid chest
Press back up until arms are fully extended
Keep feet flat on the floor throughout
coaching_cues: Arch your upper back slightly — keep lower back neutral
Bar should touch your chest — not bounce off it
Drive your feet into the floor as you press

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.description: Targets the upper chest for a fuller chest development. A staple in any muscle building program.
instructions: Set bench to 30 to 45 degrees incline
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width
Lower bar to your upper chest
Press back up to full extension
coaching_cues: Do not go too steep — shoulders take over above 45 degrees
Control the descent
Upper chest should feel it — not your front delts

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
exercises.description: Provides constant tension through the entire range of motion. Excellent for chest isolation.
instructions: Set cables to chest height on both sides
Hold one handle in each hand and step forward
With a slight bend in elbows bring hands together
Squeeze chest at the centre
Slowly return arms to the wide starting position
coaching_cues: Lean slightly forward at the hips
The squeeze at the centre is the most important part
Never fully straighten your elbows

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: A guided pressing movement on a machine. Great for beginners learning the chest press movement safely.
instructions: Adjust the seat so handles are at chest height
Grip the handles with palms facing forward
Press forward until arms are nearly extended
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Do not lock out your elbows fully
Squeeze your chest at full extension
Control the weight on the way back

exercises.name: Chest Dip
exercises.description: A compound bodyweight movement on parallel bars. Leaning forward targets the chest.
instructions: Grip the parallel bars and support your weight
Lean your torso slightly forward
Lower your body until upper arms are parallel to floor
Push back up to starting position
coaching_cues: Lean forward to target chest — stay upright for triceps
Do not go too deep
Full lockout at the top

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: Targets the upper chest through a fly movement on an incline bench.
instructions: Set bench to 30 to 45 degree incline
Hold dumbbells above chest with slight elbow bend
Open arms wide feeling a stretch in upper chest
Bring dumbbells back together above chest
coaching_cues: Go slow on the way down
Do not use too much weight
Squeeze at the top like you are crushing something between your hands

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Press
exercises.description: A decline pressing movement that targets the lower chest for complete chest development.
instructions: Set bench to a slight decline
Secure your feet under the pad
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width
Lower bar to lower chest and press back up
coaching_cues: Lower chest should feel the work
Keep a tight arch in your upper back
Do not let the bar drift toward your neck

exercises.name: Pull Up
exercises.description: One of the best upper body exercises. Builds serious back width and bicep strength using your own bodyweight.
instructions: Hang from a bar with hands shoulder width apart palms facing away
Pull your body up until chin is above the bar
Slowly lower yourself back to a full hang
Keep core tight and avoid swinging
coaching_cues: Think of pulling your elbows toward your hips
Full hang at the bottom
Squeeze your back at the top

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.description: A horizontal pulling movement under a table or low bar. A great beginner alternative to the pull up.
instructions: Lie under a table or low bar
Grip the edge with hands shoulder width apart
Keep your body straight from head to toe
Pull your chest up to the bar or table edge
Slowly lower back down
coaching_cues: The more horizontal your body the harder it gets
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top
Do not let your hips sag

exercises.name: Superman Hold
exercises.description: A lower back strengthening exercise that also activates the glutes. Important for spinal health.
instructions: Lie face down with arms extended overhead
Simultaneously lift your arms and legs off the floor
Squeeze your glutes and lower back
Hold at the top then slowly lower down
coaching_cues: Think of making yourself as long as possible
Do not hold your breath
Keep your neck neutral — look at the floor

exercises.name: Single Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A unilateral back exercise that builds thickness and corrects muscle imbalances between sides.
instructions: Place one knee and hand on a bench for support
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand hanging straight down
Pull the dumbbell up to your hip keeping elbow close
Squeeze your back at the top
Slowly lower back down then switch sides
coaching_cues: Drive your elbow toward the ceiling
Do not rotate your torso
Full stretch at the bottom

exercises.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A bilateral rowing movement that builds back thickness. Requires core stability.
instructions: Hold dumbbells with a hip width stance
Hinge at the hips until torso is nearly parallel to floor
Let dumbbells hang straight down
Pull both dumbbells to your hips simultaneously
Slowly lower back down
coaching_cues: Keep your back flat — no rounding
Soft bend in knees throughout
Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top

exercises.name: Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.description: A dumbbell version of the deadlift. One of the most effective full body exercises you can do at home.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells in front of your thighs
Hinge at the hips pushing them back
Lower dumbbells along your legs keeping back flat
Drive hips forward to return to standing
Squeeze glutes at the top
coaching_cues: Push the floor away — do not just pull the weight up
Keep dumbbells close to your legs throughout
Neutral spine — do not round your lower back

exercises.name: Band Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Mimics the lat pulldown machine using a band anchored overhead. Builds back width at home.
instructions: Anchor the band overhead to a door frame or high point
Kneel or sit and grip the band with both hands
Pull the band down toward your chest
Slowly return to the starting position
coaching_cues: Pull your elbows toward your hips
Lean back slightly as you pull down
Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the pull

exercises.name: Band Seated Row
exercises.description: A seated rowing movement with a band. Builds back thickness and improves posture.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended
Loop the band around your feet and hold both ends
Sit tall and pull the band toward your stomach
Squeeze your shoulder blades together
Slowly extend arms back to starting position
coaching_cues: Do not round your back as you pull
Elbows stay close to your sides
Sit tall throughout

exercises.name: Band Face Pull
exercises.description: Targets the rear delts and upper back. Excellent for improving posture and shoulder health.
instructions: Anchor band at face height
Hold with both hands and step back to create tension
Pull the band toward your face with elbows high
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Elbows should be at or above shoulder height
Pull toward your nose — not your chin
This is a health exercise — do not go too heavy

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: The king of all exercises. A full body compound movement that builds total body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet hip width apart bar over mid foot
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs
Keep chest up and back flat
Drive through the floor and pull the bar up your legs
Lock hips and shoulders out at the top
Lower the bar with control
coaching_cues: Push the floor away — think leg press not pull
Keep the bar touching your legs the whole way up
Take a big breath and brace your core before every rep

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A machine exercise that builds back width. Great for beginners working toward their first pull up.
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and secure thighs under pads
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width
Pull the bar down to your upper chest
Slowly return to full arm extension
coaching_cues: Lean back slightly as you pull down
Pull your elbows toward your hips
Full stretch at the top — let your lats lengthen

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: A cable rowing exercise that builds back thickness and improves posture.
instructions: Sit at the cable row machine with feet on the platform
Grip the handle and sit tall
Pull the handle toward your stomach
Squeeze shoulder blades together
Slowly extend arms back to full stretch
coaching_cues: Do not lean too far back — stay upright
Elbows stay close to your sides
Full stretch at the front

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.description: A heavy rowing movement that builds serious back thickness. A favourite of bodybuilders for decades.
instructions: Stand over the T-bar with feet on the platform
Hinge forward until torso is at 45 degrees
Pull the bar to your chest
Squeeze your back hard at the top
Slowly lower back to full arm extension
coaching_cues: Keep your back flat throughout
Lead with your elbows not your hands
Chest should nearly touch the pad at the top

exercises.name: Machine Row
exercises.description: A guided rowing movement on a machine. Safe and effective for building back thickness.
instructions: Adjust the chest pad so you can reach the handles
Grip the handles and pull toward your body
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end
Slowly return to the starting position
coaching_cues: Do not shrug your shoulders — keep them down
Feel your back doing the work — not your arms
Full range of motion on every rep

exercises.name: Cable Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: An isolation exercise for the lats. Targets back width with straight arms for a pure lat contraction.
instructions: Set cable to the highest position
Hold the bar with straight arms at head height
Pull the bar down to your thighs keeping arms straight
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Arms stay straight throughout — this is not a row
Feel your lats contract as you pull down
Hinge slightly at the hips for better lat engagement

exercises.name: Barbell Bent Over Row
exercises.description: A heavy compound row that builds serious back thickness and overall body strength.
instructions: Hold barbell with overhand grip hip width
Hinge at hips until torso is nearly parallel to floor
Pull bar to your lower chest or upper stomach
Squeeze your back at the top
Slowly lower back to full arm extension
coaching_cues: Keep your back flat — no rounding whatsoever
Pull toward your belt buckle not your chest
Brace your core like you are about to take a punch

exercises.name: Pike Push Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight overhead pressing movement. The closest thing to a shoulder press without any equipment.
instructions: Start in a push up position then walk feet toward hands
Form an inverted V shape with your hips high
Lower the top of your head toward the floor
Push back up to the starting position
coaching_cues: The more vertical your body the more shoulder work
Head goes between your hands — not in front
Keep your core tight throughout

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
exercises.description: A wall supported handstand hold that builds serious shoulder strength and stability.
instructions: Place hands on floor about 6 inches from the wall
Kick up into a handstand with heels against the wall
Keep arms fully extended
Hold the position for target time
Come down carefully under control
coaching_cues: Push through the floor actively
Keep your core tight and body as straight as possible
Look at the floor between your hands

exercises.name: Decline Push Up
exercises.description: A push up with feet elevated that shifts emphasis to the upper chest and front shoulders.
instructions: Place feet on an elevated surface like a chair or bench
Get into push up position with hands on the floor
Lower your head toward the floor
Push back up to starting position
coaching_cues: The higher your feet the more shoulder involvement
Keep your core tight — hips should not sag
Control the descent

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A fundamental overhead pressing movement for building shoulder size and strength.
instructions: Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height
Palms facing forward elbows at 90 degrees
Press the dumbbells straight up overhead
Slowly lower back to shoulder height
coaching_cues: Do not arch your lower back — keep core tight
Press the dumbbells up in a slight arc toward each other
Full lockout at the top

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.description: The best isolation exercise for building wider shoulders. Targets the side deltoid directly.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides
With a slight bend in elbows raise arms out to the sides
Raise until arms are parallel to the floor
Slowly lower back to your sides
coaching_cues: Lead with your elbows — not your hands
Think of pouring a jug of water at the top
Go lighter than you think — form breaks down fast

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Targets the rear deltoid and upper back. Essential for balanced shoulder development and good posture.
instructions: Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back
Hold dumbbells hanging below your chest
Raise arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend
Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top
Slowly lower back down
coaching_cues: Keep your back flat
Elbows stay slightly bent throughout
Think of spreading your wings

exercises.name: Band Shoulder Press
exercises.description: An overhead pressing movement using a resistance band. Builds shoulder strength at home.
instructions: Stand on the band with feet shoulder width apart
Hold the band at shoulder height with palms forward
Press overhead until arms are fully extended
Slowly lower back to shoulder height
coaching_cues: Keep your core tight
Full lockout at the top
Control the band on the way down

exercises.name: Band Lateral Raise
exercises.description: A band version of the lateral raise. Provides constant tension for great side delt activation.
instructions: Stand on the band with one foot
Hold the other end at your side
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height
Slowly lower back down
Complete all reps then switch sides
coaching_cues: Lead with your elbow
Do not shrug your shoulder up
Slow and controlled

exercises.name: Band Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Targets the rear deltoid using a band. Helps fix rounded shoulders and improves posture.
instructions: Hold the band in front of you at chest height
With straight arms pull the band apart
Open arms wide squeezing shoulder blades together
Slowly return hands to centre
coaching_cues: Keep arms as straight as possible
Feel the squeeze between your shoulder blades
Do high reps for best results

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: The gold standard shoulder exercise. Builds strong shoulders and a powerful core.
instructions: Hold barbell at shoulder height with hands just outside shoulders
Brace core and press the bar straight up overhead
Lock out at the top
Lower back to shoulder height with control
coaching_cues: Squeeze your glutes and core as you press
Bar should travel in a straight line
Push your head through the window at the top

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Provides constant tension throughout the lateral raise. Superior to dumbbells for side delt isolation.
instructions: Set cable to the lowest position
Stand sideways and hold the cable with the far hand
Raise arm out to the side to shoulder height
Slowly lower back down
Complete all reps then switch sides
coaching_cues: Keep a slight bend in the elbow
Do not lean to the side
The cable creates tension at the bottom — use it

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A guided overhead press on a machine. Safe and effective for building shoulder size.
instructions: Adjust seat height so handles are at shoulder level
Press handles straight up until arms are extended
Slowly lower back to starting position
coaching_cues: Do not lock out fully
Control the descent
Keep your back against the pad throughout

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: Isolates the rear deltoid using cables. Essential for complete shoulder development.
instructions: Set both cables to the highest position
Cross your hands and grab the opposite cable
Pull arms apart and back in a wide arc
Squeeze rear delts at the end
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Keep a slight bend in both elbows
Think of spreading your wings
Light weight — focus on the squeeze

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: A rotating shoulder press invented by Arnold Schwarzenegger. Hits all three heads of the deltoid.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing you
As you press up rotate palms to face forward
Fully extend arms overhead
Reverse the rotation as you lower back down
coaching_cues: The rotation is what makes this exercise unique — do not skip it
Slow and controlled on the way down
Full range of motion on every rep

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.description: A pulling movement that targets the traps and side delts. Builds a thick, full looking upper body.
instructions: Hold a barbell or dumbbells in front of thighs
Pull the weight up toward your chin
Keep elbows higher than hands throughout
Slowly lower back down
coaching_cues: Do not pull the bar to your nose — chin height is enough
Elbows lead the movement
Avoid if you have shoulder impingement

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: Targets the rear delts and rotator cuff. One of the best exercises for long term shoulder health.
instructions: Set cable to face height
Hold the rope with both hands and step back
Pull the rope toward your face with elbows high and wide
Squeeze rear delts at the end
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Elbows must be at or above shoulder height
Pull toward your nose — not your chin
This should be in every workout for shoulder health

exercises.name: Tricep Dips
exercises.description: A fundamental tricep exercise using a chair or bench. Builds the back of the arms effectively.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a chair with hands gripping the edge
Slide off and lower your body by bending elbows
Lower until upper arms are parallel to the floor
Push back up to starting position
Keep back close to the chair throughout
coaching_cues: Keep your back close to the chair
Elbows point straight back — not flaring out
Do not go too deep — protect your shoulders

exercises.name: Close Grip Push Up
exercises.description: A narrow push up that shifts emphasis to the triceps. Great for building arm thickness at home.
instructions: Start in push up position with hands close together
Lower your chest toward your hands
Keep elbows close to your body throughout
Push back up to starting position
coaching_cues: Elbows stay close to your ribs — not flaring wide
Feel the triceps doing the work not the chest
Go slower to increase difficulty

exercises.name: Diamond Push Up
exercises.description: Hands in a diamond shape that targets the triceps heavily. One of the hardest bodyweight tricep exercises.
instructions: Form a diamond shape with index fingers and thumbs
Place hands in the centre under your chest
Lower chest toward your hands
Push back up keeping elbows close
coaching_cues: Elbows pointing back throughout
This is harder than it looks — start with fewer reps
Feel the tricep burning at the top

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.description: An overhead extension that stretches the long head of the tricep for maximum development.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell with both hands overhead
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending elbows
Keep elbows pointing forward and close together
Press back up to full extension
coaching_cues: Elbows should not flare out wide
Feel the stretch in your triceps at the bottom
Full lockout at the top

exercises.name: Tricep Kickback
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that fully contracts the tricep at the top of the movement.
instructions: Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back
Hold dumbbell with upper arm parallel to floor
Extend forearm back until arm is fully straight
Squeeze tricep hard at full extension
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Upper arm stays parallel to the floor throughout
The squeeze at the top is everything
Go light — form breaks down fast with heavy weight

exercises.name: Lying Tricep Extension
exercises.description: Also called a skull crusher with dumbbells. Builds tricep mass through a long range of motion.
instructions: Lie on a bench or floor holding dumbbells above your chest
Bend elbows to lower dumbbells toward your forehead
Keep upper arms vertical and still
Press back up to full extension
coaching_cues: Upper arms should not move — only forearms
Lower slowly
Full lockout at the top

exercises.name: Band Tricep Pushdown
exercises.description: Mimics the cable pushdown machine using a band. Excellent for tricep isolation at home.
instructions: Anchor band at head height above you
Hold the band with both hands at chest level
Push hands down until arms are fully extended
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Elbows stay pinned at your sides
Squeeze triceps at full extension
Do not lean forward — stay upright

exercises.name: Band Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.description: A band version of the overhead tricep extension. Targets the long head of the tricep.
instructions: Stand on the band and hold the other end behind your head
Start with elbows bent overhead
Press hands up to full extension
Slowly lower back behind your head
coaching_cues: Keep elbows close together overhead
Full extension at the top
Feel the stretch in triceps at the bottom

exercises.name: Band Kickback
exercises.description: A tricep kickback using a band for constant tension and a full squeeze at extension.
instructions: Anchor band at a low point
Hinge forward holding the band
Upper arm parallel to floor
Extend forearm back until arm is straight
Squeeze hard then slowly return
coaching_cues: Upper arm stays still
The squeeze at full extension is the point
Light resistance — control every inch

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Pushdown
exercises.description: The most popular tricep exercise in the gym. Provides constant cable tension for a great pump.
instructions: Set cable to the highest position
Hold the bar or rope with hands at chest level
Push down until arms are fully extended
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Elbows stay pinned at your sides
Squeeze at full extension
The rope allows you to flare hands out at the bottom for extra contraction

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.description: A heavy tricep exercise using an EZ bar. One of the best mass builders for the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar above your chest
Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending elbows
Keep upper arms vertical and still
Press back up to full extension
coaching_cues: Upper arms stay vertical — only forearms move
Lower slowly and in control
Have a spotter if using heavy weight

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.description: A compound pressing movement with a narrow grip that heavily targets the triceps.
instructions: Lie on bench and grip barbell with hands shoulder width
Lower bar to your lower chest
Keep elbows close to your body throughout
Press back up to full extension
coaching_cues: Narrower grip than bench press but not too close
Elbows tracking back not flaring out
Feel the triceps doing most of the pressing

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Extension
exercises.description: A cable overhead tricep extension that stretches and contracts the long head of the tricep.
instructions: Set cable to the lowest position
Face away and hold the rope overhead
Extend arms overhead to full lockout
Slowly lower the rope behind your head
coaching_cues: Keep elbows close together overhead
Feel the stretch at the bottom
Full lockout at the top

exercises.name: Machine Tricep Dip
exercises.description: A guided dip machine that is safer than parallel bar dips. Great for beginners building tricep strength.
instructions: Adjust the seat and grip the handles
Press down until arms are fully extended
Slowly return to starting position
coaching_cues: Stay upright for more tricep focus
Full extension at the bottom
Control the weight on the way up

exercises.name: EZ Bar Skull Crusher
exercises.description: A skull crusher using an EZ bar for reduced wrist strain. A staple mass builder for the triceps.
instructions: Lie on bench holding EZ bar above chest
Lower bar toward forehead by bending elbows
Keep upper arms fixed and vertical
Press back up to full extension
coaching_cues: EZ bar is easier on wrists than straight bar
Upper arms stay still throughout
Slow controlled descent every rep

exercises.name: Single Arm Cable Pushdown
exercises.description: A unilateral pushdown that corrects strength imbalances between arms.
instructions: Set cable to highest position
Hold the handle with one hand
Push down until arm is fully extended
Slowly return to starting position
Complete all reps then switch arms
coaching_cues: Keep elbow pinned at your side
Do not rotate your torso
Squeeze tricep hard at full extension

exercises.name: Chin Up
exercises.description: A pull up with an underhand grip that shifts more emphasis to the biceps. One of the best bicep exercises.
instructions: Hang from a bar with hands shoulder width palms facing you
Pull your body up until chin is above the bar
Squeeze your biceps at the top
Slowly lower back to a full hang
coaching_cues: Underhand grip means more bicep
Full hang at the bottom for maximum range
Control the descent

exercises.name: Inverted Curl
exercises.description: A bodyweight curl performed under a table. Builds bicep strength without any equipment.
instructions: Lie under a table and grip the edge with palms facing up
Hang with arms fully extended
Pull your chest up toward the table
Slowly lower back down
coaching_cues: Keep your body straight throughout
Focus on squeezing your biceps as you pull up
The closer your grip the more bicep involvement

exercises.name: Isometric Bicep Hold
exercises.description: A static bicep contraction using your own hand as resistance. Builds mind muscle connection.
instructions: Hold one arm at 90 degrees as if doing a curl
Place your other hand on top and push down
Resist the push with your curling arm
Hold the tension for the target time
Switch arms

Slight squat position with feet shoulder width
Step sideways keeping tension in the band
Bring feet back together after each step
Complete reps in one direction then reverse
coaching_cues: Stay low throughout — do not stand up between steps
Keep the band taut at all times
Feel the outer glute burning

exercises.name: Band Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge movement using a band. Trains the hamstrings and glutes at home without weights.
instructions: Stand on the band holding both ends
Hinge at the hips pushing them back
Lower hands along legs keeping back flat
Drive hips forward to return to standing
coaching_cues: Push your hips back as far as possible
Keep your back flat throughout
Feel the hamstring stretch at the bottom

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.description: The king of leg exercises. Builds total lower body mass and strength like nothing else.
instructions: Step under the bar and place it across your upper back
Grip the bar and step out with feet shoulder width
Take a breath brace your core and squat down
Keep chest up and knees tracking over toes
Drive through your heels to stand
coaching_cues: Big breath and brace before every rep
Break at the hips and knees simultaneously
Drive your knees out as you squat down

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: A machine exercise that allows heavy leg loading without the spinal demand of squats.
instructions: Sit in the machine with feet shoulder width on the platform
Release the safety and lower the platform toward your chest
Push back to near full extension
Do not lock out fully at the top
coaching_cues: Do not let your lower back lift off the pad
Feet higher on the platform means more glute
Never lock your knees fully at the top

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.description: A machine exercise that isolates the quadriceps. Great for finishing and detail work.
instructions: Sit in the machine with ankles behind the pad
Extend legs until straight squeezing quads at the top
Slowly lower back to starting position
coaching_cues: Squeeze hard at the top of every rep
Slow on the way down
Avoid if you have knee pain

exercises.name: Leg Curl
exercises.description: A machine exercise that isolates the hamstrings. Essential for balanced leg development.
instructions: Lie face down on the machine with ankles under the pad
Curl legs up toward your glutes
Squeeze hamstrings at the top
Slowly lower back to starting position
coaching_cues: Keep hips pressed into the bench
Squeeze at the top — do not just swing the weight
Full range of motion every rep

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.description: A machine squat that targets the quads intensely with less spinal load than a barbell squat.
instructions: Position yourself in the hack squat machine
Feet shoulder width on the platform
Lower until thighs are below parallel
Drive through heels to push back up
coaching_cues: Keep your back flat against the pad
Do not let knees cave inward
Go deep — this machine allows great depth

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge movement using a barbell. One of the best hamstring and glute exercises in the gym.
instructions: Hold barbell in front of thighs with overhand grip
Hinge at the hips pushing them back
Lower bar along your legs keeping back flat
Feel the hamstring stretch
Drive hips forward to return to standing
coaching_cues: Push hips back as far as possible
Keep bar close to your legs throughout
Neutral spine — no rounding

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.description: A walking lunge that builds serious leg mass and coordination. Can be done with or without dumbbells.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides or hands free
Step forward and lower back knee to the floor
Push through front heel and bring back foot forward
Continue walking forward alternating legs
coaching_cues: Stay tall — do not lean forward
Front knee stays above ankle
Long steps for more glute — short steps for more quad

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: The foundation of glute training. Activates and builds the glutes with zero equipment.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent feet flat on floor
Drive through heels and lift hips toward the ceiling
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top
Hold for a second then lower back down
coaching_cues: Squeeze your glutes as hard as possible at the top
Do not hyperextend your lower back
Drive through your heels — not your toes

exercises.name: Donkey Kick
exercises.description: A glute isolation exercise on all fours. Targets the glute max directly for shape and activation.
instructions: Start on all fours with wrists under shoulders
Keep knee bent at 90 degrees
Kick one leg back and up toward the ceiling
Squeeze glute at the top
Lower with control and repeat
Complete all reps then switch legs
coaching_cues: Hips stay square to the floor — do not rotate
The squeeze at the top is everything
Keep your core engaged throughout

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A unilateral glute bridge that increases the difficulty and fixes strength imbalances between sides.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent foot on floor
Extend the other leg straight
Drive through the planted heel and lift hips
Squeeze glute at the top
Lower back down and repeat
Switch legs after all reps
coaching_cues: Keep hips level — do not let one side drop
Squeeze as hard as you can at the top
Extended leg stays straight throughout

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: A hip thrust holding a dumbbell for added resistance. Builds glute size and strength at home.
instructions: Sit with upper back against a bench or sofa
Place a dumbbell on your hips and hold it in place
Drive through heels and thrust hips upward
Squeeze glutes hard at the top
Lower back down with control
coaching_cues: Upper back rests on the bench — not your neck
Drive through the heels
Full hip extension at the top — squeeze hard

exercises.name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
exercises.description: A wide stance squat holding a dumbbell. Shifts emphasis to the glutes and inner thighs.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder width toes pointed out
Hold one dumbbell with both hands between your legs
Lower into a squat keeping chest up
Push through heels and squeeze glutes to stand
coaching_cues: Wider stance means more glute activation
Knees track over toes — push them out
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge that targets the glutes and hamstrings. One of the best posterior chain exercises.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of thighs
Hinge at hips pushing them back
Lower dumbbells along legs with flat back
Feel the stretch in hamstrings and glutes
Drive hips forward to stand
coaching_cues: Push hips back — not just bending forward
Keep dumbbells close to your legs
Squeeze glutes at full hip extension

exercises.name: Banded Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A glute bridge with a band around the knees for extra glute activation and abductor engagement.
instructions: Place band just above knees
Lie on back knees bent feet flat
Push knees out against the band
Drive through heels and lift hips
Squeeze glutes at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: Keep pushing knees out against the band throughout
The band forces the glutes to work harder
Do not let knees cave inward

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
exercises.description: A lateral movement that activates the outer glutes and hip abductors.
instructions: Place band around ankles
Slight squat position feet shoulder width
Step sideways keeping tension in the band
Bring feet back to shoulder width after each step
Complete steps in one direction then reverse
coaching_cues: Stay low throughout
Keep tension in the band at all times
Feel the outer glute burning — that is the target

exercises.name: Banded Donkey Kick
exercises.description: A donkey kick with a band around the ankle for added resistance and better glute activation.
instructions: Place band around one ankle and anchor the other end under your knee
Start on all fours
Kick the banded leg back and up against the resistance
Squeeze glute at the top
Complete all reps then switch legs
coaching_cues: Hips stay square — do not rotate
Squeeze at the top every single rep
Slow and controlled — feel the glute working

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: The most effective glute exercise in existence. Builds glute mass and strength like no other movement.
instructions: Sit with upper back against a bench
Roll a barbell over your hips
Drive through heels and thrust hips upward
Squeeze glutes as hard as possible at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: Upper back on the bench — not neck or lower back
Full hip extension at the top — not half reps
Chin tucked — look at your belly button at the top

exercises.name: Cable Kickback
exercises.description: A cable glute kickback that provides constant tension for excellent glute isolation.
instructions: Attach ankle strap to cable at the lowest position
Face the machine holding it for support
Kick the cable leg back and up
Squeeze glute at the top
Lower with control and repeat
Switch legs
coaching_cues: Keep a slight bend in the standing knee
Do not swing — control the movement
Feel the glute squeezing — not your lower back

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description: A wide stance deadlift that shifts more emphasis to the glutes and inner thighs than a conventional deadlift.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than shoulder width toes pointed out
Hinge down and grip the bar inside your legs
Drive through the floor pushing knees out
Lock hips and back at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: Push your knees out hard throughout the lift
Keep chest up and back flat
Drive the floor apart with your feet

exercises.name: Glute Machine
exercises.description: A dedicated glute machine that isolates the glutes safely and effectively.
instructions: Adjust the machine for your height
Place working leg on the pad
Drive leg back and up against the resistance
Squeeze glute at full extension
Return with control
coaching_cues: Full range of motion every rep
Squeeze hard at the top
Do not use momentum — control the movement

exercises.name: Cable Pull Through
exercises.description: A hip hinge using a cable that targets the glutes and hamstrings with constant tension.
instructions: Face away from the cable machine
Hold the rope between your legs
Hinge forward pushing hips back
Drive hips forward squeezing glutes to stand
Let the rope pull back between your legs for the stretch
coaching_cues: This is a hip hinge — not a squat
Feel the glute and hamstring stretch at the bottom
Powerful hip extension at the top

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
exercises.description: A hip thrust using the Smith machine for a guided, stable movement. Great for beginners learning the hip thrust.
instructions: Set up bench perpendicular to the Smith machine
Rest upper back on bench with bar on hips
Drive through heels and thrust hips up
Squeeze glutes hard at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: The Smith machine keeps the bar path controlled
Same cues as barbell hip thrust
Great option if you struggle to balance a free barbell

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: The foundation of core training. Builds deep core stability that carries over to every other exercise.
instructions: Start on your forearms with elbows directly under shoulders
Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe
Push the floor away with your forearms
Hold for the target time
Breathe steadily — do not hold your breath
coaching_cues: Imagine pulling your elbows toward your feet
Do not let hips sag or pike up
Look at the floor — keep your neck neutral

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: A dynamic core exercise that targets the obliques and rectus abdominis simultaneously.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands behind your head
Bring one knee to your chest
Rotate your opposite elbow toward that knee
Alternate sides in a cycling motion
Keep lower back pressed to the floor
coaching_cues: Do not pull your neck — hands are just resting
Slow is better — feel the oblique working
Full rotation — bring elbow all the way across

exercises.name: Leg Raise
exercises.description: A lower abdominal exercise that builds core strength and hip flexor endurance.
instructions: Lie on your back with legs straight
Place hands under your lower back for support
Raise legs to 90 degrees keeping them straight
Slowly lower back toward the floor without touching
Keep lower back pressed down throughout
coaching_cues: Do not let your lower back arch off the floor
Slow on the way down — that is where the work is
Keep legs straight throughout

exercises.name: Dumbbell Russian Twist
exercises.description: A weighted rotation exercise that targets the obliques for a strong defined core.
instructions: Sit with knees bent feet slightly off the floor
Hold one dumbbell with both hands
Lean back slightly and rotate side to side
Touch the dumbbell to the floor on each side
coaching_cues: Keep your chest up — do not collapse forward
Rotate from your torso — not just your arms
Feet off the floor makes it harder

exercises.name: Weighted Crunch
exercises.description: A weighted crunch that adds resistance to the basic crunch for progressive ab development.
instructions: Lie on your back knees bent feet flat
Hold a dumbbell on your chest
Curl your upper body toward your knees
Squeeze abs at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: Do not pull your neck — hold weight on chest
Short range of motion — you do not need to sit all the way up
Exhale as you crunch up

exercises.name: Farmers Carry
exercises.description: Walking while holding heavy dumbbells. Builds full body strength grip and core stability simultaneously.
instructions: Pick up heavy dumbbells and stand tall
Keep core tight and shoulders back
Walk forward taking controlled steps
Keep the dumbbells from swinging
Set down with control at the end
coaching_cues: Stand as tall as possible — do not lean
Brace your core like you are about to be punched
Take short controlled steps

exercises.name: Band Pallof Press
exercises.description: An anti-rotation core exercise. Trains the core to resist rotation rather than produce it — essential for spine health.
instructions: Anchor band at chest height to the side
Hold band at your chest with both hands
Stand sideways to the anchor point
Press hands straight forward holding for a second
Return hands to chest with control
coaching_cues: Resist the band pulling you sideways — that is the exercise
Keep your hips square and still
Do not let the band rotate your torso

exercises.name: Band Woodchop
exercises.description: A rotational core exercise that mimics a chopping motion. Builds oblique strength and rotational power.
instructions: Anchor band at head height on one side
Hold band with both hands
Pull the band diagonally across your body toward opposite hip
Rotate through your torso
Return slowly to starting position
Complete all reps then switch sides
coaching_cues: The rotation comes from your core — not your arms
Keep your feet planted throughout
Control the band on the way back

exercises.name: Band Crunch
exercises.description: A resisted crunch using a band for progressive ab training at home.
instructions: Anchor band overhead
Hold the band behind your head
Curl forward against the resistance
Squeeze abs at the bottom
Return to upright with control
coaching_cues: Pull with your abs — not your arms
Short controlled range of motion
Exhale as you crunch down

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.description: A weighted crunch using a cable. Allows progressive overload for the abs like any other muscle.
instructions: Kneel facing the cable machine
Hold the rope behind your head
Curl down bringing elbows toward knees
Squeeze abs hard at the bottom
Return to upright with control
coaching_cues: The movement is from your abs — not your hips
Do not pull with your arms
Round your back as you crunch down

exercises.name: Ab Rollout
exercises.description: One of the most challenging core exercises. Builds extreme core strength and stability.
instructions: Kneel on the floor holding an ab wheel
Roll forward as far as you can keeping core tight
Use your abs to pull yourself back to start
Do not let your hips sag at full extension
coaching_cues: Start with partial reps if full extension is too hard
Brace your core before you start rolling
Pull back with your abs — not your arms

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: Hanging from a bar while raising your legs. One of the most challenging and effective ab exercises.
instructions: Hang from a pull up bar with straight arms
Raise your legs keeping them straight
Bring them as high as possible
Lower with control without swinging
coaching_cues: Avoid swinging — control every rep
Tuck your pelvis as you raise your legs
Bent knee version is easier if needed

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.description: A rotational cable exercise that builds oblique strength and rotational power.
instructions: Set cable at head height
Hold handle with both hands
Pull diagonally across body toward opposite hip
Rotate through the torso
Return slowly and repeat
Switch sides after all reps
coaching_cues: Rotation from the core — not the arms
Keep feet planted and hips stable
Control the cable on the return

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
exercises.description: A crunch on a decline bench that increases the range of motion and difficulty.
instructions: Secure feet on a decline bench
Cross arms over chest or hands behind head
Curl your upper body toward your knees
Squeeze abs at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: Do not pull your neck
Full range of motion — go all the way up and all the way down
Slow on the way down

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
exercises.description: An advanced full body core exercise. Requires serious strength and is not for beginners.
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head
Raise your entire body as one rigid unit
Lower slowly keeping body straight
Stop just before your body touches the bench
Raise back up
coaching_cues: Your entire body should stay rigid like a plank
The lowering phase is the hardest part
Start with tucked knees if full version is too hard

exercises.name: Cable Pallof Press
exercises.description: An anti-rotation cable exercise that builds core stability and spinal health.
instructions: Set cable at chest height
Stand sideways and hold handle at chest
Press arms straight forward
Hold for a second then return
Resist the cable pulling you sideways
coaching_cues: Hips stay square and still
The resistance you are fighting is the exercise
Switch sides after all reps

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.description: The ultimate full body conditioning exercise. Builds cardiovascular fitness and burns maximum calories.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder width
Drop hands to floor and jump feet back to plank
Lower chest to floor
Push up and jump feet back toward hands
Jump up with arms overhead
coaching_cues: Move fast but stay in control
Land softly to protect your joints
Scale by stepping instead of jumping if needed

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.description: A running in place exercise that elevates heart rate quickly. Great for warm up or cardio circuits.
instructions: Stand with feet hip width apart
Run in place driving knees as high as possible
Pump arms in opposition to legs
Stay on balls of feet throughout
coaching_cues: Drive knees above hip height for full benefit
Stay light on your feet — do not stomp
Pump your arms to increase intensity

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
exercises.description: A classic cardio exercise that elevates heart rate with minimal impact. Great for warm ups and circuits.
instructions: Stand with feet together arms at sides
Jump feet out wide while raising arms overhead
Jump back to starting position
Repeat at a steady rhythm
coaching_cues: Land softly on each jump
Keep a slight bend in knees throughout
Arms fully overhead on each rep

exercises.name: Dumbbell Thruster
exercises.description: A squat to press combination. One of the most efficient full body exercises that builds strength and burns calories.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height
Lower into a squat
As you stand drive the dumbbells overhead
Lower dumbbells back to shoulders as you squat again
coaching_cues: Use the momentum from the squat to help drive the press
Full squat depth and full lockout overhead
This should be hard — that is the point

exercises.name: Dumbbell Man Maker
exercises.description: The most demanding dumbbell complex. A full body movement that combines a push up row and thruster.
instructions: Hold dumbbells on the floor shoulder width
Jump feet back to plank position
Do a push up
Row each dumbbell up in turn
Jump feet back toward hands
Stand and perform a thruster
coaching_cues: Each rep is a full workout in itself
Go lighter than you think — this destroys everyone
Control every part of the movement

exercises.name: Dumbbell Swing
exercises.description: A dumbbell version of the kettlebell swing. Builds powerful glutes and burns serious calories.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder width holding a dumbbell vertically
Hinge at hips and swing dumbbell back between legs
Drive hips forward explosively
Let the dumbbell swing up to chest height
Control it back down and repeat
coaching_cues: This is a hip hinge — not a squat
Power comes from your hips — not your arms
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top

exercises.name: Band Squat Jump
exercises.description: A banded squat jump that adds resistance to explosive jump training for power and fat loss.
instructions: Stand on the band holding it at shoulder level
Lower into a squat
Explode upward jumping as high as possible
Land softly and go straight back into the squat
coaching_cues: Land with soft knees — absorb the impact
Maximum effort on every jump
The band makes the squat harder — the jump is your power

exercises.name: Band Mountain Climber
exercises.description: Mountain climbers with a band around the feet for added resistance and core tension.
instructions: Loop band around both feet
Get into a plank position
Drive one knee toward your chest against the band resistance
Alternate legs quickly
coaching_cues: Keep hips level — do not pike up
The band adds resistance to each drive
Core stays tight throughout

exercises.name: Band Lateral Shuffle
exercises.description: A lateral shuffling movement with a band around the ankles. Builds agility and burns calories.
instructions: Place band around ankles
Slight squat position feet shoulder width
Shuffle sideways quickly for target distance or time
Reverse direction and repeat
coaching_cues: Stay low throughout
Quick feet — this should feel like sport
Keep tension in the band at all times

exercises.name: Rowing Machine
exercises.description: A full body cardio machine that is low impact and burns serious calories. One of the best cardio options.
instructions: Sit on the machine and secure your feet
Grip the handle and sit tall
Push through your legs first
Then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your chest
Reverse the sequence to return to start
coaching_cues: Legs first — then lean — then pull
Do not round your back
Aim for a steady rhythm throughout

exercises.name: Treadmill Sprint
exercises.description: Sprint intervals on a treadmill. One of the most effective fat burning cardio methods.
instructions: Set treadmill to sprint speed
Sprint for the target time
Step to the sides to rest
Repeat for target sets
coaching_cues: Sprint as hard as you can during the work period
Full recovery between sprints
Increase speed over time as fitness improves

exercises.name: Stair Climber
exercises.description: Continuous stair climbing on a machine. Burns calories while building lower body endurance.
instructions: Step onto the machine and hold the rails lightly
Set a comfortable speed
Step continuously for the target time
Stay upright — do not lean too far forward
coaching_cues: Do not lean on the rails — that reduces calorie burn
Drive through your heels for more glute engagement
Steady pace beats going too fast and stopping

exercises.name: Battle Ropes
exercises.description: Explosive rope wave exercises that build upper body endurance and burn maximum calories.
instructions: Hold one rope end in each hand
Slight squat position feet shoulder width
Alternate raising each arm creating waves in the rope
Move as fast as possible for target time
coaching_cues: Waves should travel all the way to the anchor
Stay in the squat position throughout
Breathe — do not hold your breath

exercises.name: Assault Bike
exercises.description: A fan bike that uses both arms and legs simultaneously. One of the most brutal conditioning tools available.
instructions: Sit on the bike and grip the handles
Pedal feet and push pull arms simultaneously
Sprint as hard as possible for target time
Rest fully between intervals
coaching_cues: Push and pull with the arms — do not just use legs
Sprint intervals are most effective on this machine
The harder you go the harder it gets — there is no ceiling

exercises.name: Jump Rope
exercises.description: Jumping rope for cardio. Cheap portable and burns serious calories. One of the best conditioning tools.
instructions: Hold one handle in each hand
Swing the rope overhead and jump over it
Stay on the balls of your feet
Keep jumps small and fast
coaching_cues: Small jumps are more efficient than big ones
Wrists do the work — not your whole arms
Find your rhythm and stick to it

exercises.name: Barbell Squat
exercises.description: The most important lower body exercise in existence. Builds total body mass and strength.
instructions: Bar across upper back feet shoulder width
Big breath brace and squat
Chest up knees tracking over toes
Drive through heels to stand
coaching_cues: Brace your core before every rep
Break at hips and knees simultaneously
Drive knees out throughout

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: The king of all exercises. Builds total body strength like nothing else in existence.
instructions: Bar over mid foot feet hip width
Hinge down grip bar outside legs
Chest up back flat
Push floor away as you lift
Lock hips and shoulders at top
coaching_cues: Push the floor away — leg press the ground
Bar stays against your legs throughout
Big brace before every rep

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: The upper body pressing benchmark. Builds chest shoulder and tricep strength.
instructions: Eyes under bar grip slightly wider than shoulders
Arch upper back feet flat on floor
Lower bar to mid chest
Press back to lockout
coaching_cues: Arch upper back — keep lower back neutral
Bar touches chest — no bounce
Drive feet into floor as you press

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: A full body pressing movement. Builds shoulder strength and requires total body tension.
instructions: Bar at shoulder height grip just outside shoulders
Brace core and press bar straight up
Lock out overhead
Lower back to shoulders with control
coaching_cues: Squeeze glutes and core as you press
Push head through the window at the top
Bar moves in a straight vertical line

exercises.name: Pull Up
exercises.description: The upper body squat. Builds back width and overall upper body strength.
instructions: Hang with overhand grip shoulder width
Pull up until chin clears the bar
Lower to a full hang
Keep core tight throughout
coaching_cues: Pull elbows toward your hips
Full hang at the bottom every rep
No kipping — strict form only

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.description: A compound upper body pushing movement. Builds chest and triceps simultaneously.
instructions: Grip parallel bars and support your weight
Lean forward slightly for chest focus
Lower until upper arms parallel to floor
Push back up to lockout
coaching_cues: Lean forward for chest — stay upright for triceps
Do not go too deep — protect your shoulders
Full lockout at the top

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.description: The primary horizontal pulling movement. Builds back thickness and overall upper body strength.
instructions: Overhand grip hip width hinge to 45 degrees
Pull bar to lower chest or upper stomach
Squeeze back at the top
Lower to full extension
coaching_cues: Flat back — absolutely no rounding
Pull to your belt buckle not your chest
Brace core like you are about to take a punch

exercises.name: Lunge
exercises.description: A fundamental unilateral lower body movement. Builds leg strength and corrects imbalances.
instructions: Stand with feet together
Step forward and lower back knee toward floor
Front thigh parallel to floor
Push through front heel to return
Alternate legs
coaching_cues: Front knee stays above ankle
Stay tall — do not lean forward
Back knee almost touches the floor

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: The most effective glute exercise. Builds glute size and strength directly.
instructions: Upper back on bench barbell on hips
Drive through heels thrust hips upward
Squeeze glutes hard at the top
Lower with control
coaching_cues: Full hip extension at the top
Chin tucked at the top position
Drive through heels not toes

exercises.name: Max Effort Burpee
exercises.description: As many burpees as possible in the time window. The ultimate way to end a session and burn maximum calories.
instructions: Set a timer for the target time
Perform as many burpees as possible
Do not stop — push through the burn
Count your reps and try to beat it next time
coaching_cues: Pace yourself for the first 20 seconds
Push hardest in the last 20 seconds
Every rep counts — do not stop

exercises.name: Plank Hold
exercises.description: A max effort plank hold to finish the session. Builds core endurance and mental toughness.
instructions: Get into a forearm plank position
Hold for as long as possible
Focus on breathing steadily
Do not let your hips sag or pike
coaching_cues: Squeeze everything — glutes core shoulders
Breathe slowly and steadily
When it burns the most is when it matters the most

exercises.name: Wall Sit Hold
exercises.description: A max effort wall sit to finish a lower body session. Builds quad endurance and mental toughness.
instructions: Slide down the wall until thighs are parallel to the floor
Hold for as long as possible
Keep back flat against the wall
Do not let your knees cave inward
coaching_cues: Thighs parallel to the floor — not higher
Keep your hands off your legs
Breathe through the burn — it will pass

exercises.name: Mountain Climber Sprint
exercises.description: Maximum speed mountain climbers to spike the heart rate at the end of a session.
instructions: Get into a plank position
Drive knees to chest as fast as possible alternating legs
Go as fast as you can for the full time
Do not let your hips rise
coaching_cues: Hips stay level — do not pike up
As fast as possible — this is a sprint
Drive your knees all the way to your chest

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.description: Explosive squat jumps to finish the session on a power note. Burns out the legs and spikes the heart rate.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder width apart
Lower into a squat
Explode upward jumping as high as possible
